title: Crossing the 12,000-atom barrier with heterogeneous quantum-classical supercomputing: quantum chemistry of protein-ligand complexes
summary: We develop a workflow decomposing a molecule into fragments via quantum embedding and simulating them with a heterogeneous quantum-classical (HQC) method. We sample fragment electronic configurations on two 156-qubit quantum processors (ibm$\_$cleveland, ibm$\_$kobe), using up to 94 qubits, running 21,006 circuits for over 239 hours, collecting $3.0 \cdot 10^9$ measurement outcomes -- the most resource-intensive HQC computation for quantum chemistry to date.
